why: Both analyses propose nearly the same home-state, low-cost, profit-per-employee hedgehog, name all four key brutal facts, and tell the bank to stop growth-for-size, new ventures and energy/shipping/developing-country lending, so they are hard to separate on substance. Analysis 2 edges ahead with an explicit confidence statement, a sharper decline warning (under-reserved losses followed by an acquisition or new-state push as the cure, with concrete trigger thresholds), and attention to size-based incentives and unknown capital adequacy.
